round1_to_round2.summary: Every agent adopted the round-1 corrections (consensus $4.16, guided >=3.72B lb, ~31-32% tax, ~38-40% NCI share, $5.3B net debt, NCI valued at ~$51-54B in EV legs, front-month COMEX premium gone). Fair values converged from a $60-72 range to $63-68 (mean $66.0 -> $65.4) and the ladders now sit within about +/-0.02 of each other; the mean ladder barely moved (P>=71 0.480 -> 0.475). The remaining spread is almost entirely the copper deck ($5.60-6.15). Source overlap rose (mean Jaccard 0.075 -> 0.182, distinct share 0.826 -> 0.685) because all five now cite the same supervisor-verified originals (Q2 8-K/10-Q, Yahoo, SMM Sep 29), so the round-2 agreement is partly shared information, not five independent confirmations.

revision_check.note: Did everything asked: Q3 consensus $0.74, tariff re-expressed as LME overhang, attributable FCF share 65%->62%, NCI 40%. Fixed its own EBITDA slope to the $13-20B endpoints. Remaining issue: treats management's $5-7 model as a 2027-only figure and then adds 8-10% for 2028; the model is the 2027-28 average, so its 2027 EPS is ~$0.15-0.2 high and its 2028 leg double counts half the ramp.

Fixed tax (38%->31%), net debt ($5.3B), NCI (market value at 38% share), multiple (18x->16.5x). Added a genuinely new in-lane fact: ICSG's June 2026 forecast is a refined surplus (96kt 2026, 377kt 2027), replacing a stale deficit claim. Its $5.60 deck is now the lowest; its 2028 EBITDA adds ~$1.2B on top of a model that already averages 2027-28.

Moved volume to guidance, rebuilt EV leg with consistent NCI, $5.90 deck, verified NCI shares itself. 2028 EBITDA adds ~$1.45B to the 2027-28-average model (double count). Its statement that NCI makes attributable earnings 'much less copper-levered' is the wrong direction: the 0%-NCI US mines are the high-cost, most price-sensitive assets, so the NCI share rises when copper falls.

Fixed tax/NCI, rebuilt EV leg (NCI ~$52B), added FCF leg, and brought new in-lane Indonesian-language sources (200k tpd by 2027, Manyar restart, export permit not renewed). Its partial disagreement on the COMEX overhang is supported by the primary SMM text and is accepted.

Replaced the $2.80 run-rate EPS with a model-based $3.70/$4.00, dropped the discounted Substack/DB/Kalshi inputs, downgraded the n=4 analogues and reran conditional base rates (median -2%, log-sd 0.51, n=54 overlapping). EBITDA at $5.75 ($15.4B) is a bit below the linear $15.6B; 2028 adds ~$1.1B on top of the 2027-28-average model.

disagreements.positions: 2027(-28) decks: agent_1 $6.15, agent_4 $6.10, agent_3 $5.90, agent_5 $5.75, agent_2 $5.60 (spot $6.56, LME-level). All five now use the same ~$3.5B EBITDA per $1/lb slope from management's $13B@$5 / $20B@$7 model (agent_5 slightly below linear).
disagreements.resolution: The method is now consistent; the levels are judgment calls. A $0.55/lb spread is worth ~$10/share and explains almost all of the $63-68 fair-value spread. None of the decks is wrong on evidence: consensus $4.16 maps to ~$6.00-6.25 on the shared bridge, while Goldman/Cochilco-style forecasts ($5.10-5.50) support the lower decks. I could not obtain a current 2027 futures curve, so I do not overrule any deck. The one real inconsistency is elsewhere: management's model is the AVERAGE of 2027 and 2028, not 2027 alone. Agents 1 and 4 treat it as 2027 (2027 EPS ~$0.15-0.2 too high), and agents 2, 3 and 5 add $1.1-1.45B on top of it for 2028 (about half of that is double counted, ~$0.15-0.2 EPS or ~$2.5-3/share at 16x). Used as the NTM proxy at the Sep-2027 horizon (which spans ~3 quarters of 2028), the model figure itself is about right. Gold in the model is $4,000/oz vs $4,155 spot, worth only ~$0.16B EBITDA.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 call: modelled results use the 'average of 2027 and 2028' at current volume/cost estimates, gold flat $4,000/oz, moly $30/lb; ~$13B EBITDA/$9.5B OCF at $5, $20B/$15.5B at $7; $390M per $0.10. Trading Economics gold $4,155 on Sep 30.

disagreements.positions: All five now use a 38% (agent_1 40%; agents 3 38%/40% 2028) NCI share of net income, 61-62% attributable FCF, and deduct NCI at ~38% of equity value (~$51-54B) in the EV legs.
disagreements.resolution: Consistent across agents and consistent with the evidence at a ~$6 deck: 2026 guidance is NCI ~$2.0B, ~24% of pretax income (~34% of net income at a 30% ETR) with Grasberg impaired, and a full-Grasberg 2027-28 mix lifts that to ~38-40%. What no agent models is that the share moves with price: US mines (1.4B lb of 3.1B lb in 2026) are 100% owned and the highest-cost, so at lower copper the NCI share rises (52% in H1 2025 at $4.48 Cu with full Grasberg) and at higher copper it falls (33% in H1 2026 at $6.04). On the shared bridge, a $5 deck with a ~43-44% NCI share gives ~$2.7 EPS rather than the ~$2.95-3.1 the agents use, so their bear scenarios ($44-45) are ~$3-4 too high; a $7 deck at ~35% gives ~$5.2 rather than ~$5.0. Attributable EPS is therefore MORE copper-levered than a constant-NCI bridge implies, mostly on the downside.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 8-K Ex. 99.1: NCI $913M of $2,778M H1-26 (realized Cu $6.04, Au $4,704); $1,216M of $2,340M H1-25 (Cu $4.48, Au $3,260); 2026 NCI guide ~$2.0B (~24% of pretax); 2026 sales U.S. ~1.4B lb, S. America ~1.0B lb, Indonesia ~0.7B lb; PTFI 48.76%, Cerro Verde 55.66%, El Abra 51% owned.

disagreements.topic: Is the COMEX tariff / warehouse-stock risk adequately in the bear tail?
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2, 3, 5 put the ~770k st COMEX stock returning to LME (if the tariff is dropped) into a 25% bear scenario at $44-45 with ~$5 copper. agent_4 treats it as smaller and slower, citing SMM on re-export costs.
disagreements.resolution: The bear tail is adequate, and agent_4 is right that the overhang is slow: SMM's primary text says re-export is costly and tariff expectations have turned US stocks into a 'quasi-strategic reserve'; ex-US stocks are tight (LME ~250kt from 400kt in April, SHFE 47kt, China social 78kt, cathode premiums highest since Oct 2023). A formal drop would therefore hit LME gradually, not in a July-2025-style one-day COMEX collapse (and the front-month COMEX premium is already gone, so FCX's US realized price has no premium left to lose). Two things are missing: (1) the tariff is two-sided for FCX, because an enacted 15% tariff lifts COMEX-priced US sales (~1.4B lb) and is a right-tail item only agents 3 and 4 mention; (2) the NCI convexity above makes the $5-copper outcome ~$40-41, not $44-45. The mean ladder's left tail (P<49 ~22%, P<42 ~14%) is close to agent_5's conditional base rate (log-sd 0.51 gives ~25%/~16%), which includes FCX's leveraged 2008 and 2015 episodes, so only a small fattening is warranted.
disagreements.evidence: SMM Sep 29, 2026 (two notes): COMEX ~770k st vs ~320k st a year ago; Oct-26 -$46.94/t, Nov-26 +$38.99/t vs LME 3M; proposal 15% 2027 / 30% 2028; Reuters Sep 10 (plan stalled over affordability).

The copper-deck disagreement is judgment that I could not settle with a current forward curve. summary: Round 2 converged: all five agents adopted the round-1 corrections, fair values narrowed to $63-68 (mean $65.4) and the ladders sit within ~0.02 of each other with a median near $69-70, just below the $70.58 spot. The copper-deck ($5.60-6.15) and NCI (~38%, ~$51-54B in EV legs) treatments are now methodologically consistent; the remaining errors are second order: management's $13-20B model is a 2027-28 average (agents 2, 3, 5 double count part of the 2028 ramp), and a constant NCI share understates downside because the 100%-owned US mines are the high-cost assets. The COMEX-stock/tariff risk is adequately in the bear tail and is slower than feared (SMM: re-export is costly), while an enacted tariff would be upside for FCX's COMEX-priced US sales. I make only a small left-tail fattening (confidence low); FCX remains a fairly priced, high-beta copper position with Q3 results ~Oct 22 as the next event.

On a ~$10,000 portfolio (cash already included) a single ~45-48%-vol cyclical should not exceed ~8% (~$800); a fall to the $47 thesis break would cost ~2.7% of the portfolio. Liquidity is no concern (NYSE mega-cap), but Q3 earnings and the undecided tariff argue for staging the entry.
